AutoSave_OfflineOnlyNotice: Auto-save runs offline only. While connected to a server, saving stays manual.
Common_CopyTooltip: Duplicate this record into the first empty slot. The copy is not saved until you save it.
Common_CopyNeedsRecord: This slot is empty — there is nothing here to copy.

AssetManager_Empty: No sheets here yet. Import one to get started.
AssetManager_UsagePartial: Used by {Maps} of the loaded map(s), {Tiles} tile(s)
AssetManager_UsageNonePartial: Not used by any loaded map
AssetManager_ProblemDuplicate: Index {Index} is claimed by more than one file ({Files}). Only one of them loads, and which one is decided by the filesystem.
AssetManager_ProblemNoIndex: {File} has no index in front of its name, so it is not loaded at all.
AssetManager_ProblemOutOfRange: {File} claims index {Index}, past the last usable index of {Max}. It is not loaded.
AssetManager_ProblemNotAligned: {File} is not a whole number of {Size}px tiles. The leftover strip holds cells nothing can select.
AssetManager_ProblemNoAlpha: {File} is a PNG with no transparency in it. PNGs are not color-keyed, so it will draw as a solid block.
AssetManager_ProblemMissingSize: Sheet #{Index} ({File}) has no counterpart at this size. NPCs with that footprint draw no sprite at all.
AssetManager_ProblemSizeRows: {File} holds a different number of sprites than sheet #{Index} does at 32x32. The same number has to be the same character at every size.
AssetManager_ConsequenceTiles: Tiles painted with it will render blank, and in the game they will cast a full square of shadow instead of their own shape.
AssetManager_ConsequenceSprites: NPCs, classes, and characters that name it will draw no sprite at all.
AssetManager_ConsequenceItems: Items that name it will draw no icon, on the ground or in a bag.
AssetManager_ConfirmRestoreMoved:
Index {Was} is taken now. Restore this sheet as index {Now} instead?

Maps painted with the old #{Was} will not point at it.
AssetManager_Deleted: Moved index {Index} to the recycle bin.
AssetManager_Repaired: Renamed to {File}, now loading as index {Index}.
AssetManager_FullNoIndex: All {Max} indexes are in use. Delete a sheet to free one.
AssetManager_PickTitle: Choose a sheet to bring in
LayerVisibility_Intro: Checked means visible. Uncheck a layer to take it off the map canvas while you work on another one. Nothing here changes the map.
Console_Intro: What the editor has been logging, as it happens. Logging sets how much detail is captured; the same lines are written to a file.
WorldPreview_Hint: Click a map to open it, or its Warps badge to see where they lead. Ctrl+drag pans, Ctrl+scroll zooms.
WarpTargets_None: No Warp on this map leads anywhere new.
HelpDialog_LayerGroundDesc: Up to 5 layers drawn below players, NPCs, and items. Layer 1 is the base floor.
HelpDialog_LayerAnimFlagDesc: Tick the Anim box before painting to flag that layer as animated - it flashes on the animation tick. Works on any Ground, Fringe, or Canopy layer.
HelpDialog_LayerTilesetDesc: Each layer can use any loaded sheet; choose it from the Tileset box (type a name or index). Alt + scroll changes the active layer. See Assets and Views below for where sheets live and how they are named.
HelpDialog_LayerFringeDesc: Up to 5 layers drawn between the Ground- and Fringe-plane entity passes - the walkable surface of a bridge deck. Pair with a Layer Ramp attribute at each end so it can be mounted from Ground.
HelpDialog_LayerCanopyDesc: Up to 5 layers drawn above everything - players and NPCs on both planes (treetops, roofs, overhangs).
HelpDialog_LayersIntro: Each tile has three layer types - Ground (drawn below all entities), Fringe (the walkable bridge-deck surface, drawn between the Ground- and Fringe-plane entity passes), and Canopy (drawn above everything - treetops, roofs, overhangs) - each a stack of up to 5 layers composited bottom-to-top. Pick the layer type and number in the tools panel; right-click clears the hovered cell's selected layer, left-click fills it only if empty.
HelpDialog_SelectionIntro: Select mode lets you grab a rectangular region of the map and paste it elsewhere. The clipboard is mode-specific: a tile copy can only be pasted in Tile mode, an attribute copy only in Attribute mode. In Tile mode the source layer doesn't matter — paste always lands on the layer currently selected. Paste follows the same rule as regular placement: cells already occupied on the destination layer (or with a conflicting attribute) are skipped, and empty cells in the trimmed clipboard preserve the original gap structure.
HelpDialog_AttributesIntro: Attributes govern a tile's in-game behavior. In the two-plane world each attribute is authored on a logical layer - Ground (the base level) or Fringe (a bridge deck above it) - chosen with the Layer selector in the tools panel or Ctrl+Alt+scroll; the hover cursor shows G or F. Layer Ramp is the special connector between the planes. Right-click clears the active layer's attribute.
HelpDialog_Ctrl_LeftClickDesc: Paint tile or place attribute on hovered cell
HelpDialog_Ctrl_AltClickDesc: Place attribute with retained values, skipping the dialog (attribute mode only)
HelpDialog_Ctrl_CtrlDragDesc: Pan the map canvas by dragging
HelpDialog_Ctrl_CtrlAltShiftClickDesc: Switch to the surrounding map at the clicked cell — same as selecting it in the map list. If the clicked cell is a Warp tile on the active (center) map, jumps to the warp's destination map instead. No-op on an empty cell or on the active map with no warp under the cursor.
HelpDialog_Ctrl_RightClickDesc: Clear the active tile layer or remove attribute
HelpDialog_Ctrl_BackForwardDesc: Navigate back / forward through previously selected maps. Every map switch (list pick, neighbor click, or warp jump) is pushed onto the history stack.
HelpDialog_Ctrl_MouseBackForwardDesc: The side buttons on most modern mice — wired to the same Back / Forward navigation.
HelpDialog_Ctrl_ShiftHoldDesc: Show the exploded tile view — per-layer indices and attribute for the hovered cell (suppressed while Ctrl is held)
HelpDialog_Ctrl_AltScrollWheelDesc: Step the active layer index (number) up or down within the current layer type (clamped to 1-5).
HelpDialog_Ctrl_CtrlAltScrollWheelDesc: Change the active layer, clamped (no wrap). Tile mode cycles the layer type (Ground / Fringe / Canopy); Attribute & Light mode flips the logical plane (Ground / Fringe). The hover cursor shows the current layer - e.g. G4 / F1 in Tile mode, G / F in Attribute mode.
HelpDialog_Ctrl_SaveMapDesc: Write the selected map (or all dirty maps) to disk
HelpDialog_Ctrl_DiscardMapDesc: Reload the selected map (or all dirty maps) from disk, discarding unsaved changes
HelpDialog_Ctrl_PaletteClickDesc: Click a tile to use it as the brush; drag a rectangle on the tile palette to grab a multi-tile region as the brush.
HelpDialog_Sel_ActionPlaceDesc: Default action mode. Left-click stamps the selected tile (Tile mode) or attribute (Attribute mode). Drag continues stamping along the path.
HelpDialog_Sel_ActionSelectionDesc: Left-click and drag on the map to outline a rectangular selection (bright white). The selection lives only on the current map and clears if you switch maps.
HelpDialog_Sel_CtrlCSelectionDesc: Copy the selection to the clipboard. Tile mode copies only the currently selected layer; Attribute mode copies the attribute type and its data fields. The clipboard is automatically trimmed to the smallest rectangle containing real content, preserving internal gaps. The selection rectangle clears after copying. If nothing was copyable the existing clipboard is left untouched.
HelpDialog_Sel_ActionDeleteDesc: Brush-erases the active content (tile-art layer, attribute, or light — by mode) under an adjustable brush. Like right-click, but sized.
HelpDialog_Sel_CtrlXSelectionDesc: Cut — copies the selection then clears those cells (Tile mode clears the selected layer; Attribute mode clears the attribute). Undoable in one step.
HelpDialog_Sel_ModeKeysDesc: Switch edit mode: Tile, Attribute, or Light (reads left to right).
HelpDialog_Sel_ClickPlaceDesc: Pastes the clipboard at the cursor. Clipboard is cleared after the paste.
HelpDialog_Sel_CtrlShiftClickDesc: Pastes the clipboard and retains it for re-pasting. The exploded tile view is suppressed while Ctrl is held, so the preview is unobstructed.
HelpDialog_Sel_EscDesc: Select mode: clears the selection rectangle. Place mode: clears the clipboard. With a Warp/Item Spawn/Key dialog open: closes the dialog.
HelpDialog_Attr_BlockedDesc: Hard wall. Neither players nor NPCs can enter this tile.
HelpDialog_Attr_WarpDesc: Teleports the player the moment they step on it. Set the destination map, X, and Y. The player arrives at exactly those coordinates.
HelpDialog_Attr_ItemDesc: Spawns a floor item that players can pick up. After collection it respawns after the configured delay. Respawn Seconds 0 uses the server default (120 s).
HelpDialog_Attr_ItemData: Data: Item · Value · Respawn Seconds (0 = 120 s default)
HelpDialog_Attr_NpcAvoidDesc: Passable for players, but NPCs will not path through it.
HelpDialog_Attr_DoorDesc: Blocks movement until a player possessing the required item interacts with the tile. Once unlocked, all players on the map can pass through. The door re-locks after 5 seconds. If 'Take key on use' is checked, the key item is consumed on unlock.
HelpDialog_Attr_DoorRevealDesc: Door reveal: paint the door's top graphic on the highest Ground layer, with a floor or base on the layers below it, then mark the tile Door. When the door is open only the topmost populated Ground layer is hidden (revealing what sits beneath); use the toolbar Doors toggle to preview the open state in the editor.
HelpDialog_Attr_DoorData: Data: Key Item · Take on use (0 = keep, 1 = consume)
HelpDialog_Attr_PlateDesc: A trigger tile. Stepping on it automatically unlocks the Door tile at the specified coordinates — no item required.
HelpDialog_Attr_PlateData: Data: Door Tile X · Door Tile Y (coordinates of the Door tile on this map)
HelpDialog_Attr_NpcSpawnDesc: Pins a map NPC slot to this tile so it always spawns here instead of a random walkable tile. Click an eligible (non-empty, unpinned) slot in the NPC Slots list to place it; right-click a pinned tile to clear it.
HelpDialog_Attr_LayerRampDesc: The connector between the two logical planes - the 'hole' between the Ground level and a Fringe bridge deck above it. A ramp is solid on the ground (you cannot walk under or through it) and walkable only on the Fringe surface, so the only way onto a bridge is up a ramp from its Ground-side foot. Place it on a fully clear tile (it cannot share a tile with any other attribute on either plane) and set the Ground-side direction. Occupies both planes; right-click removes it from either.
HelpDialog_Attr_LayerRampData: Data: Ground-side direction (the low end you mount from)

MapEditor_LightModeHint: Click a tile to place or edit a light. Right-click removes it. Copy and paste work like attributes.
MapEditor_ClearLightsTooltip: Remove all placed light sources from this map.
MapEditor_InheritHint: Indoors, Always Lit, and Always Dark are tri-state: checked = on, unchecked = off, dash = inherit from the map group. Always Lit and Always Dark are exclusive — ticking one returns the other to inherit.
MapEditor_DoorPreviewTooltip: Toggle previewing Key doors as open (topmost Ground layer hidden) or closed.
MapEditor_NightPreviewTooltip: Preview how this map renders at night, with placed light sources active.

MapEditor_AttrDesc_Blocked:
{Name}

Hard wall. Neither players nor NPCs can walk onto this tile. Use it for invisible collision on decorative tiles that have no natural edge.
MapEditor_AttrDesc_NpcAvoid:
{Name}

Passable for players, but NPCs will refuse to path through it. Useful for shaping wander zones or preventing NPCs from chasing players into safe areas.
MapEditor_AttrDesc_Door:
{Name}

Blocks movement until a player with the required item uses it to unlock. Once unlocked the door opens for all players on the map and re-locks after 5 seconds. The key item can optionally be consumed on use.

Door graphic: paint the closed-door tile on this cell's highest Ground layer, with a floor or base on the layers below it. While the door is open the client hides that topmost Ground layer (revealing what sits beneath) to simulate it opening, then restores it when it re-locks.

Data stored: Key Item # · Take on use (0/1)

DoorTileDialog_KeyItemTooltip: Item the player must possess to unlock this tile.
DoorTileDialog_TakeKeyTooltip: If checked, the key item is removed from the player's inventory when this door is unlocked.

MapResize_Intro: How many tiles this map is, across and down. Tiles that fall outside the new size are discarded.
MapResize_LinkedRefusal: This map is linked to map {Maps}, so it cannot be resized. Every map joined by an edge must be the same size, or a step across the seam lands somewhere other than where it looks. Clear the links first, or settle on a size before joining a zone up.
MapResize_SoftCapWarning: Past {Cap} tiles on an axis. Nothing breaks - larger maps just cost load time and memory. Crossing a seam loads three maps and a lost NPC searches all nine: about 40 ms each at 128x128, about 180 ms at 256x256. A 128x128 map is 1.5 MB resident against 24 KB for the default.
MapResize_Irreversible: This cannot be undone or restored by any means. Copy the world folder first if you might want any of it back.
MapResize_LossPins: {Count} NPC spawn pin(s) will be cleared
MapResize_LossWarps: {Count} warp(s) on other maps will point at nothing
MapEditorStatus_Resized: Map resized to {Width} x {Height}. Save to keep it.
SchemaEditor_NoFields: This family declares no fields, so there is nothing to fill in. Its records can still be created, copied and saved.
SchemaEditor_MissingRequired: Some required fields are still empty.
ItemEditor_Notes_EquipmentDurability: • Durability: what the piece starts with when it is picked up or given. What spends it is the game's rule; the engine only enforces the ends — at 0 the piece comes off, stays in the bag, and cannot be worn again until a repair shop restores it. 0 = no durability budget, so it never wears.
ItemEditor_Notes_EquipmentPower: • Power: a number carried on the piece. The engine reads it only to price the item and to charge for repairs; what it does to a character is the game's to decide.
ItemEditor_Notes_EquipmentSlot: • Worn in: which of the game's equipment slots this piece occupies. One item per slot, and a piece naming no slot — or one this world does not declare — is carried rather than worn.
ItemEditor_Notes_ConsumableAmount: • Amount: a number the item carries. The engine hands it to the game’s rule and has no opinion about what it counts — restoring something, spending something, or nothing at all. The item is used up on use, on a clock the engine paces.
ItemEditor_Notes_KeyId: • A key carries no fields of its own. Key-type tiles in the map editor name the item that opens them by ITEM NUMBER, so this item’s own slot number is its key id — different key items open different doors. Whether the key is consumed is set on the tile, not here.
ItemEditor_Notes_CurrencyDesc: • Stacks: picking up currency adds to an existing stack rather than filling a new inventory slot. No Data fields are used — the quantity is tracked by the inventory slot's value field.
ShopEditor_SalesHint: Priced from the item itself, so the same goods cost the same at every vendor — use a barter trade when one must differ. The order here is the order players see.
ShopEditor_SalesSummary: {Items} stocked, {Gold} gold to buy the lot
ShopEditor_SalesWarnDuplicate: The same item is listed twice — the duplicate is dropped when this shop is saved.
ShopEditor_SalesWarnNoPrice: An item here has no price, so the shop hands it over for nothing.

AccountEditor_NoCharacters: This account has no characters yet.

AccountEditor_SelfAccessHint: This is your own account - access is locked.
ConversationEditor_GraphHint: Click a node to edit it. Wheel to zoom, drag to pan, double-click to reset.
EntityEditor_Copied: Copied {EntityType} {From} into slot {To}. Not saved yet.
EntityEditor_NoEmptySlot: No empty slot left — every one of the {EntityTypePlural} is in use.
MapGroupEditor_SelectPrompt: Select a map group to edit
MapGroupEditor_FallbackHeader: Fallback properties (a map's own value overrides these)
MapGroupEditor_TriStateHint: Checkboxes: checked = on, unchecked = off, dash = do not set (a map inherits it).
NpcEditor_DropWarnChanceNoItem: Drop chance is set but no item is selected; this NPC drops nothing.
NpcEditor_DropWarnItemNoChance: A drop item is set but the drop chance is 0; it will never drop.

Logging_DialogIntro: The editor writes a log file each day. Raise the capture level when you are chasing a problem, and lower it again afterwards — the detailed levels produce large files.
Logging_LevelErrorDetail: Failures alone. Smallest files, and the least to go on when something goes wrong.
Logging_LevelWarningDetail: Failures, plus anything that degraded and carried on — a render that fell back, a stalled interface.
Logging_LevelInformationDetail: Enough to reconstruct a session: connections, records loaded and written, navigation, edits, dialogs.
Logging_LevelDebugDetail: Adds every request and response to the server, and the detail behind each action. Large files.
Logging_LevelVerboseDetail: Everything, down to the per-frame heartbeat. Very large files — for reproducing one specific fault.
World_NotFound: That world is no longer at {Path}.
World_EmptyHint: Open a world folder to start editing, or connect to a server.
WorldSettings_Intro: How many of each record this world has room for. Lowering a number hides the slots above it; nothing is deleted, and raising it again brings them back.
WorldSettings_NameHint: What to call this set of records. Shown in the editor and the server window - never to a player.
WorldSettings_GameNameHint: What players see this game called, in their window title, menus and HUD. Leave it empty and players see the engine's name. An operator running a server may override it for their own installation. It never affects file or folder names.
WorldSettings_DefaultMapSizeHint: The size a new map starts at, in tiles. Any map can be resized afterwards in its properties.
WorldSettings_MapSizeSoftCapWarning: Past {Cap} tiles on an axis. Nothing breaks - larger maps just cost load time and memory, and every map in a linked zone has to match. Crossing a seam loads three maps and a lost NPC searches all nine, so both grow with the map.
WorldSettings_OfflineOnlyNotice: Connected, the record ceilings are the server's. Open a world folder to change these.
WorldTransfer_TargetNotEmpty: {Path} already holds a world. Downloading replaces every record in it. Continue?
WorldTransfer_NoChanges: {Path} matches the server. Nothing to upload.
WorldTransfer_Summary: {Added} to add, {Changed} to change, {Removed} to blank.
WorldTransfer_BackupAdvice: Back up the server's world folder before uploading. This overwrites records in place and there is no undo.
WorldTransfer_RemovalsWarning: These records are authored on the server and blank in {Path}. Uploading them blanks the server's copy. A folder that never held them looks exactly the same as one they were deleted from, so leave this off unless you meant to remove them.
WorldTransfer_IncludeRemovals: Also blank the {Count} records listed below
WorldTransfer_OverCeiling: {Count} records in this folder sit above the server's ceiling and cannot be uploaded. Raise the server's record limits to take them.
BlockedTileDialog_Description: Nothing walks through a blocked tile. What else it stops is up to you — a solid wall stops everything, a railing or a window stops neither.
BlockedTileDialog_BlocksLightTooltip: Marked, this tile shades in the shape of its own art — light passes wherever the graphic is clear. Unmarked, a lamp behind it still lights the ground in front of it.
BlockedTileDialog_BlocksSightTooltip: Off, you can see straight through it - it still stops anyone walking into it.
Common_FillConnectedRun: Apply to the whole connected run
Common_FillConnectedRunTooltip: Every touching tile carrying this same attribute gets the same values. Available when you click one that is already there — laying a new one has no run to follow.
NpcEditor_RangeWarnTooShort: This one attacks on sight but only sees {Range} tiles, so it notices nothing until somebody is beside it. {Min} or more is usual.
NpcEditor_RangeWarnTooFar: Seeing {Range} tiles puts this one past the {Cap} a player can see up or down, so it can pick a target that never saw it coming.
NpcEditor_StandoffWarnPastReach: This one holds {Standoff} tiles off but only sees {Range}, so it will stop at the edge of its own sight instead.
HelpDialog_WorldIntro: A world is a folder of records - maps, items, NPCs, shops, conversations, and whatever kinds of record the loaded game declares - that the editor and the server both read. Everything below describes what a map is and what it inherits, which is what the map canvas is editing. World - Check World reads the whole lot back and reports anything that does not hold together.
HelpDialog_World_WorldFolderDesc: A world folder describes itself in a world.json at its root: its name, the size new maps are created at, and how many of each record it has room for. Edit all three under World - World Settings. The file is optional; a folder without one runs on the stock answers. The world name is for you, not for players - it labels the title bar, the recent-worlds list, the server window, and the logs, so a live world and a test copy of it are told apart. Players only ever see the game's name.
HelpDialog_World_MapSlotsDesc: Maps are numbered slots, 1000 of them unless the world says otherwise, and every slot is a real map whether or not anyone has drawn on it. A map's number is its identity: warps, spawn points, and links all name it. The map list shows the number, the internal Name, and the player-facing Display Name together - the Name is an authoring label, the Display Name is what the game shows.
HelpDialog_World_MapSizeDesc: A map is 16x12 tiles unless it says otherwise. The world sets what a new map starts at; any map can then be resized in its Properties. Resizing cannot be undone - shrinking discards everything outside the new bounds, so the dialog counts exactly what would go (authored tiles, lights, spawn pins, and warps pointing in from other maps) before you commit. Past 128 tiles on an axis it warns: drawing costs the same at every size, but loading a map and searching one both grow with it.
HelpDialog_World_LinksDesc: Each map names the map beyond each of its four edges. The game draws the map a player stands on together with its eight neighbors as one continuous world, so a border is just another step. The canvas shows the same 3x3: the map being edited is the center cell and the ring around it is context. Clicking outside the center navigates to that map rather than painting on it. Linked maps must all be the same size - world coordinates run straight across a seam - so resizing a linked map is refused.
HelpDialog_World_GroupsDesc: A map can name a group, and the group fills in anything the map leaves unset: music, indoors, lighting, players passing through, the exit point, and the enter/leave greeting. The map's own value always wins, so a group is a default and not an override - set a building's greeting or a dungeon's lighting once for all its rooms. A group also carries a name and display name, which sit between a map's Display Name and its Name when the game decides what to call a place.
HelpDialog_World_PropertiesDesc: Indoors stops weather falling inside. Always Lit and Always Dark override the day/night cycle and are mutually exclusive. Music names the track. Players Pass Through lets players walk through each other here, which a crowded town square wants and a narrow corridor does not. The exit point says where a player who leaves this map other than by walking ends up. Greetings are lines spoken on entering and leaving, attributed to a speaker.
HelpDialog_World_PlanesDesc: Every tile has two walkable levels: Ground, and a Fringe deck above it for bridges. Attributes, lights, and walkability are authored per plane, and a Layer Ramp is the only way between them. Whichever plane you are editing draws at full strength while the other dims. See Tile Layers and Attribute Reference above for how to paint each.
HelpDialog_ViewsIntro: Two windows sit beside the map canvas while you work. Both are opened from the View menu and stay open while you keep editing.
GeneralHelp_AssetsIntro: Art lives beside the editor rather than inside a world, so it is shared by every world you open. The Assets menu manages it, and the Reload menu re-reads it.
GeneralHelp_Assets_SheetsDesc: Tiles, sprites, and items are each numbered sets of sheets under assets/ - tiles/, sprites/32x32, sprites/64x64, sprites/96x96, and items/. A file is named with a leading index, e.g. 0_Tiles.bmp or 1_Cave.png, and that number is what every map and record stores; the name after it is yours to change freely. Both BMP and PNG are read, and the extension decides transparency: a BMP is keyed on its top-left pixel, a PNG keeps its own alpha. A sprite number means the same character at all three sizes, so 1_Beasts must exist in each size folder you use.
GeneralHelp_Assets_ManagerDesc: Assets - Manage Assets lists every sheet of a class with its size, format, and what uses it. Import takes the lowest free index, Rename changes only the name half, Replace swaps the art and keeps the index, and Delete moves the file to a recycle bin it can be restored from. It also reports the files the loader would otherwise skip in silence - no index in front of the name, two files claiming one index, an index past the last usable one - each with a button that gives the file a free number.
GeneralHelp_Assets_ReloadDesc: Reload - Reload World re-reads the records from disk and is unavailable while connected, because a server hands those out. Reload - Reload Assets re-scans the art folders and stays available online, since the graphics are this machine's and a server has no say in them.
HelpDialog_Views_WorldPreviewDesc: View - World Preview draws the maps linked to the open one, laid out as they join, out to a reach of 10 maps. Click a map to open it. Ctrl + drag pans, Ctrl + scroll zooms, Shift + scroll scrolls sideways, and the bottom-right of each map counts how many other maps its warps lead to - click that to see them.
HelpDialog_Views_LayerVisibilityDesc: View - Layer Visibility takes layers off the map canvas so you can work on one without the others over it. Checked means visible; a stack's box covers all five of its layers at once, and one button shows or hides everything. It changes only what is drawn - never the map, the World Preview, or an exported image - and painting onto a layer you have put away asks whether to bring it back first. Everything returns to visible when the window closes.
HelpDialog_Views_ConsoleDesc: View - Console shows what the editor has been logging, as it happens: connects, loads, saves, and anything that failed. It is already recording before you open it, so opening it after something odd still shows the odd thing. The same lines are written to a log file - Open log folder goes there - and Logging sets how much detail both of them capture. It only displays; there is nothing to type.
MapEditor_LinkSizeMismatch: Map {Target} is {TargetSize} and this map is {Size}. Maps joined by an edge must be the same size - world coordinates run straight across a seam, so a step across a mismatched one would land somewhere other than where it looks. Resize one of them first.
WorldCheck_Intro: Reads every record against every other and reports what does not agree. Nothing is changed.
WorldCheck_CleanNote: Every link, Warp, exit point, spawn pin, group, and record reference resolves to something that exists.
WorldCheck_LinkSizeMismatch: Linked to a map of another size: {Detail}. Maps joined by an edge must match, or a step across the seam lands somewhere other than where it looks.
WorldCheck_LinkNotReciprocal: One-way link: {Detail}. The other map does not link back, so the seam only works in one direction.
WorldCheck_LinkOutOfRange: Link to a map this world has no room for: {Detail}.
WorldCheck_WarpTileOutside: Warp to a tile its destination has not got: {Detail}. The server refuses this warp when a player steps on it.
WorldCheck_ExitTileOutside: Exit point names a tile its map has not got: {Detail}.
WorldCheck_MapGroupMissing: Belongs to group {Detail}, which has no record.
WorldCheck_SpawnPinOutside: NPC spawn pinned outside the map: {Detail}.
WorldCheck_WarpMapMissing: Warp to a map that is not there: {Detail}.
WorldCheck_ExitMapMissing: Exit point names a map that is not there: {Detail}.
WorldCheck_NpcMissing: Names NPC {Detail}, which is not there.
WorldCheck_ItemMissing: Names item {Detail}, which is not there.
WorldCheck_ConversationNodeMissing: Leads to node {Detail}, which this conversation does not contain.
WorldCheck_ShopHasNoKeeper: No keeper. A shop is opened by talking to its keeper and by nothing else, so no player can reach this one.
WorldCheck_ConversationOpensNoShop: Offers to open a shop, but NPC {Detail} keeps none - the choice does nothing when a player picks it.
World_NotAWorld: {Path} is not a world folder - it has no world.json. Use World - New World to make one, or pick a folder that already holds a world.
NewWorld_Explanation: The name is for you, not for players - it tells this world apart from a copy of it in the title bar, the server window, and the logs. It is also the folder's name: you choose where to keep it next, and the world is made in a folder of its own there.
NewWorld_Failed: The world could not be created: {Reason}
NewWorld_AlreadyThere: {Path} already exists. Give the world a different name, or keep it somewhere else.
NewWorld_InvalidName: "{Name}" cannot be a folder name. Leave out \ / : * ? " < > and |.
